entry_points.text: Work drives convergence; completion wakes the response channel and init binds the handler to one queue under a stable name for later requests.
Memory driver registers for the memory device id, advertises unplugged-inaccessible, persistent-suspend and locality capabilities, and binds probe/remove/config/freeze/restore.
MMIO probe maps and validates then registers; queue discovery takes the shared IRQ with optional wake; suspend/resume delegate to generic helpers with page-size reprogram.
Cmdline instantiation parses size/base/IRQ/optional id, builds resources, lazily registers a parent, creates incrementing platform devices, and supports readback and unregister.
Probe requires config access, loads addressing/sizing/placement with node fallback, then diverges to capture registration or full hotplug setup.

exports.text: Single-queue setup binds one caller name and completion callback to a device and reports allocation failure as an error pointer.
Transport feature filtering keeps understood ring bits and unified creation builds packed or split rings from negotiation.
Shared interrupt service reports used-entry presence and broken state and builds notify values from queue identity and position.
Queue teardown detaches under lock; coherent allocation and release prefer a device map interface then generic or paged paths.
Address queries expose descriptor and driver/device event locations, selecting packed stored addresses or split base plus offsets.

hazards.text: Shrink eligibility probes run lockless and may race online/offline activity; staleness is benign because retirement revalidates.
Misaligned or out-of-span device extent only warns and may leave edge memory unusable, surfacing later as address-space exhaustion.
Name duplication avoids stale pointers on force-remove; reservation failure warns that reload is unsupported and aborts busy.
Work in capture kernels logs once and returns untouched; an unrecognized completion code terminally marks the device broken.
Bad config widths and zero status are fatal; legacy setup fails above the 32-bit frame range and modern deactivation failure only warns.
Removal cannot revoke added system RAM and only warns when its range still contributes RAM.
Paged allocation derives device address from CPU address and fails with a one-time warning on narrowing; address queries abort unless the ring is owned.
Big-block states are ADDED, FAKE_OFFLINE, PLUGGED, UNUSED; small-block states are PLUGGED, UNUSED, MOVABLE_PARTIAL, KERNEL_PARTIAL, OFFLINE_PARTIAL.
State use REQ_STATE with ACK carrying PLUGGED/UNPLUGGED and ERROR for rejection; request channel is guest-request with retry bounds MIN_MS to MAX_MS doubled per expiry.

invariants.text: A big region is offline only if no slice backs an online page; it is movable if every online slice is in the movable zone.
Shrinkage converts bytes to whole big regions and reaps high to low preferring offline then movable then any added region; mode flag selects small or big handling.
Config refresh mirrors plugged size, bounds usable span by device and pluggable limits, derives the last usable unit with downward rounding, then reloads requested size.
Small-block mode is chosen when subblock extent is below OS block size without forcing; first unit rounds up from the covered start and offline threshold covers two units.
Setup creates parent resource, dynamic group, notifiers and device before ready; teardown publishes removing state, cancels work, unregisters, then releases only if no RAM remains.
Config change is ignored in capture mode else flags work; freeze refuses plugged suspend without persistence, restore rebuilds the queue and replays config handling.
Features transfer as high then low halves; legacy generation reads zero, status uses the low byte, zero status is refused, and reset polls for clear on modern versions.
Legacy config moves bytewise; modern supports 1/2/4/8 bytes with 8 as ordered halves. Notify always succeeds; data form folds queue identity with next position.
Queue deletion deactivates via frame or ready register, walks all queues on full teardown, syncs the shared IRQ, and frees owned backing plus tracking.

Queue creation records identity, callback and ordering, derives indirect/event/layout from features, forces strong barriers under platform order, inits counts, chains extras, and publishes no-interrupt when callbackless.
Timer expiry reschedules work with doubling bounded delay; device state tracks active and pending-config flags around each pass.
State queries report plugged state on ack and map device error distinctly; capture classification treats outside span as normal RAM and enumeration coalesces plugged chunks.

locks.text: Retirement holds the hotplug mutex across fake-offline marking and restore; teardown publishes removal under an IRQ-safe spinlock before cancelling work.
Small-block retries hold the hotplug mutex, combine per-block status, and retain a pending flag; work tracks active and pending-config indicators.
Capture classification and full enumeration hold the hotplug mutex; enumeration stages into a temp list spliced on success or discarded on failure.
Queue list linkage and removal use the device queue-list spinlock; MMIO callback sync waits for the shared platform IRQ handler.

state_machines.text: Big-block retirement needs added on entry, passes through fake-offline while quiescing, ends unused on success or plugged if host release fails late, else restores added.
Work suppresses in capture/broken states, honors full-release and config flags, converges toward requested size; results reset backoff, pause, rearm, rerun, or mark broken.
Cleanup asks the host to release lingering plugged units toward unused, with small-block mode retrying partially unplugged movable/kernel/offline units.
Probe builds sync state, queue and config then schedules work unless capturing; remove branches capture versus hotplug teardown, resets, deletes queues and frees state.
MMIO IRQ acks causes then dispatches config and per-queue handlers; queue setup validates name/activity/size, programs addresses, activates, and unwinds on failure.
Packed creation allocates descriptor, driver then device event areas with full unwind; split creation aborts the queue object if state allocation fails.

structs.text: Per-device state groups addressing, sizing, block management with first/next/last units, hotplug serialization, work flags, retry timing and capture cache.
MMIO transport embeds the generic device, keeps platform device and mapped base, version, and wakeup state, with a helper to recover the enclosure.
Split state keeps descriptor/avail/used pointers, count, address, shadow flag/index, free head and batch marker; packed keeps descriptor plus two event pointers, sizes, wraps and markers.
Config layout carries block extent, node, base, total and usable sizes, plus plugged size as reflection of past actions and requested size as target.
MMIO expects signature virt, versions 1-3, id 0 placeholder; SHM uses id plus length/address halves with all-ones meaning absent; discovery uses virtio,mmio and LNRO0005; rings align to page size.
Split footprint places descriptors, then avail, then aligned used with headers for flags/index/event plus per-entry used elements.
The driver reserves the whole span as exclusive system RAM under a duplicated name, clears busy for later addition, and releases idempotently on delete.
